headline: A preregistered probe finds context truncation can erase unrecoverable state in a synthetic agent task
summary: A preregistered preprint tests when agent context policies affect task success rather than only cost. In a synthetic PersistGym-lite probe, the author reports a 92.5-point difference between context-truncation penalties when a needed fact could not be re-observed versus when it could. A one-model-per-provider replication showed the same pattern but was non-confirmatory. The paper also decomposes an ARC-AGI-3 harness gap for one model on four games, with one counted run per configuration and game and post-result changes to some summary budgets. The results support a bounded author-reported case that losing unrecoverable state can matter; they do not establish general agent performance or portable harness rankings.
